name: Exosome treatments

lead: Exosomes are tiny membrane-bound vesicles released by cells, and cosmetic products marketed as exosome serums use vesicles from sources such as stem cells, often applied after microneedling to skin said to be aging or scarred.

Laboratory research on exosomes is extensive, but clinical trials of cosmetic exosome products are few and small, and registered trials in skin aging and hair loss are early-stage or have ended without results being listed.

paras: Exosomes carry proteins, lipids and nucleic acids between cells, and researchers study them as signalling carriers. Proponents of cosmetic use propose that these cargoes can signal skin cells to repair; whether functional transfer of this kind occurs in humans is described by Wikipedia as having limited definitive evidence.

In late 2019 the FDA issued an advisory about noncompliant exosome marketing and about patient injuries linked to exosome injections, stating that exosomes are drug products requiring pre-market approval. Wikipedia describes ongoing unapproved marketing of cosmetic exosome products. Products differ in source and purity.

lead: Exosome treatments are cosmetic or medical-aesthetic products that use exosomes, small extracellular vesicles of roughly 30 to 150 nanometres released by cells, typically derived from stem cells and applied to the skin, frequently after microneedling [1]. They are marketed for skin rejuvenation, scarring and hair.

Exosome biology is a major research field. A 2007 paper showed that exosomes from mast cells carry mRNAs and microRNAs that can be transferred between cells [2], and reviews describe exosomes as mediators of cell-to-cell communication [3][4]. A position statement from the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles notes that the field uses many overlapping terms for vesicle types and sets minimal reporting standards [5].

Cosmetic use is far less studied. Registered trials of exosomes with microneedling for skin aging and for hair loss exist, but no published results were identified for this article [6][7][8]. The FDA has said exosome products are drugs requiring pre-market approval [1].
infobox: FDA: exosome products are drugs requiring approval [1]

paras: Exosomes are formed inside the endosomal system of cells and released when a multivesicular body fuses with the cell membrane. Their cargo includes proteins, lipids and nucleic acids, and varies with the cell of origin [1]. Wikipedia notes it is unclear whether exosomes have unique functions or can be reliably separated from other vesicles, and that the broader term extracellular vesicle is often more accurate [1][5].
Exosomes were first identified in maturing reticulocytes in 1983 by two research groups, and the term was applied to this vesicle type in 1987 [1].

No published clinical trial results of cosmetic exosome products were loaded for this article. Registered studies include a completed phase 4 trial of topical exosomes applied with a microneedling device for facial skin aging in 30 participants, with no results listed in the registry entry [6]; an early-phase trial of exosomes for hair loss in 16 participants that was terminated [7]; and a 20-participant study of exosomes for prevention of hair loss with unknown status [8].

Outside cosmetics, Wikipedia cites animal findings, such as faster wound healing in rats with exosomes from oral keratinocytes, and early clinical trials of other exosome-based therapies, and says many therapeutic applications are preclinical or early-stage [1]. Wikipedia also states that definitive evidence of functional RNA transfer by exosomes in mammals remains limited [1].

According to Wikipedia, in late 2019 the FDA issued an advisory about noncompliant exosome marketing and patient injuries in Nebraska linked to exosome injections, and stated that exosomes are drug products requiring pre-market approval. In 2020 the agency cautioned firms about marketing exosomes for COVID-19 and other conditions. Wikipedia describes continued unapproved marketing in US clinics, including cosmetic skincare claims, though that later statement is not well cited [1].
Exosome serums are categorised on the wiki under hardmaxx as an add-on to microneedling and similar procedures. No community threads are cited in this article.
